relevance_note: Single case report of biopsy-confirmed Alexander disease ("We report a case of Alexander's disease in a black South African boy of 9 years."); no GFAP testing is reported, so the person is in scope by diagnosis and has no variant row.
method_note: Hand extraction from the Markdown; no table transcription script. One in-scope person, labelled 'patient' (rule 5). No GFAP variant or genetic testing is reported (the diagnosis rests on cerebral biopsy), so the variants table is empty and publications.n_patients_reported is null (the field counts patients with a GFAP variant). The 'six healthy siblings' and the sister who gave the history are neither tested nor described as affected, so they get no rows. Publication year is not printed (only 'Accepted 16 January 1979'), so year is null. The only age given is the age when first seen (9 years and 5 months), recorded as age at last evaluation; the Discussion's follow-up at the time of writing gives no age. Onset age is not stated (only a one-month history, which the authors thought too short). The negation 'There was no' (end of the examination paragraph) and 'evidence of incoordination, nystagmus, or ataxia.' are split by a page break and figure caption in the Markdown, so those exclusions cite both pieces as a span list. The Discussion is two columns merged line by line; only contiguous fragments were quoted (follow-up status, deterioration, posture worse). Head circumference of 570 mm is printed but not characterised by the authors, so macrocephaly is not reported. Enlarged ventricles on CT are not called hydrocephalus, so that checklist item is not reported. Spasticity or pyramidal signs marked excluded from normal tone, normal reflexes and flexor plantars. Developmental delay excluded from 'milestones were apparently normal', a hedged statement from a history the authors call inadequate. 'The systematic examination was normal' excludes nothing more specific and was not recorded as a feature. Normal laboratory results recorded as excluded abnormalities under D-27. No contradictions found.
